COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPCRL No. 589 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. J. S. Virk, learned Addl. Advocate 
General and Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned AGA 
for the State. 
3. By the instant petition, petitioner is praying 
for the following reliefs:
 
 “i. To issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to take 
immediate lawful action against the accused persons 
involved in threatening, harassing and circulating 
obscene video of petitioner's sister.
 ii. To issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing an independent 
investigation by senior officer/another agency into the 
illegal acts, omissions and misconduct of police officials 
of PS Lambgaon and PS Chamba District 
TehriGarhwal.
 iii. To issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to 
produce and preserve CCTV footage of Koti Colony 
Outpost/PS Lambgaon for the period from evening of 
09.05.2025 to 10.05.2025 in accordance with Supreme 
Court guidelines and also to produce phone location 
and call record of concern police officials as well as 
petitioner from evening of 09.05.2025 to 10.05.2025
 iv. To issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the Respondent No.3 
(State Police Complaint Authority) to decide the 
petitioner's complaint dated 06.11.2025 within a time 
bound period.”
4. In this petition, respondent nos. 4 to 11 are
police officials though they are impleaded as 
respondent party by their name and designation. 
5. Petitioner raised serious allegation against 
respondents no. 4 to 11 and he also approached to 
the State Human Right Commission and State 
Police Complaint Authority with complete  electronic evidence and petitioner has also 
attacked on the police officials by submitting that 
when no action has been taken against the erring 
police officials, therefore, he was compelled to 
raise his voice on social media and since then, 
private respondents herein are biased against him, 
consequently, he has been falsely implicated in 
multiple FIRs only to counter to his complaint 
against the police officials. On 09.05.2025, he was 
taken into police custody and shown to be 
arrested on 10.05.2025 and during this period, he 
was subjected to physical and mental torture. 
6. On 08.04.2026, this Court directed the 
respondent nos. 5 and 6 to join the proceedings 
through V.C. and preserve the CCTV footage of 
Koti Colony Outpost / PS – Lambgaon, for the 
period from 09.05.2025 to 10.05.2025 and place the 
same before this Court on the next date. 
7. In compliance of the previous order, 
respondent no. 5 – Circle Officer, Tehri Garhwal, 
joined the proceeding through V.C. and 
respondent nos. 6 and 11 are also present in the 
Court. Respondent no. 5 – Circle Officer apprise to 
this Court about the past history of the petitioner 
and his family members.
8. After gone through with the petition and 
arguments of Mr. S.K. Pandey and past history of 
the petitioner and his family members, as apprised 
by respondent no. 5 – Circle Officer, this Court is 
of the view that matter requires deep scrutiny but 
before that the police officials should proceed for 
medical check up of the petitioner, as per 
procedure laid down in Chapter XIII of the Mental 
Health Care Act, 2017. 
9. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the petitioner, submits that petitioner 
is at present residing in Dehradun and if it is so, 
then Mr. Pandey, shall give details where 
petitioner is residing to Mr. J.S. Virk, learned 
Addl. Advocate General for the State during the 
course of the day, so that police officials may take 
assistance of Dehradun police in order to proceed 
under Chapter XIII of the Mental Health Care Act, 
2017.
10. Mr. J. S. Virk, learned Addl. Advocate 
General for the State apprised to this Court that 
petitioner is repeatedly sending messages in social  media platform targeting some police officials.
11. This Court takes serious cognizance on the 
petition filed by the petitioner, therefore, Mr. S.K. 
Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioner, 
directed to advice his client not to send any 
message in social media platform targeting police 
officials and if he has any grievance, he can 
apprise to this Court at any point of time. 
12. Till the next date of listing, no coercive 
action shall be taken against the petitioner. 
13. On the next date, Mr. J.S. Virk, learned 
Addl. Advocate General shall apprise to this Court 
about the mental condition of the petitioner. 
14. List on 23.04.2026 on top of the board.
15. For the time being personal appearance of 
the police officers are exempted. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 16.04.2026
SKS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPCRL No. 589 of 2026
WPCRL No. 1000 of 2021
WPCRL No. 1613 of 2023
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey and Mr. Nalin Saun, 
learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Dy.A.G. with Mr. Bhaskar 
Chandra Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Rajat Mittal and Mr. Ayush Negi (through 
V.C.) for the petitioners in the connected writ petitions.
4. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned Deputy Solicitor 
General for India for Union of India.
5. Mr. Vipul Sharma, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
6. The petitioner of WPCRL No. 589 of 2026 Mr. 
Keshav Thalwal S/o Bolam Singh Thalwal is present
pursuant to the previous order.
7. On the previous date pursuant to the arguments 
as advanced by Mr. Virk and after seeing certain video 
clips, which was shown by Mr. Virk on his mobile, the 
police administration was directed to proceed under 
Chapter XIII of Mental Health Care Act, 2017, but 
subsequent thereto Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey apprise 
to this court that no attempt was made by the police 
administration to call upon the petitioner. 
Consequently, the petitioner was called and now 
present before this court.
8. After interaction with the petitioner for half an 
hour in open court in the presence of counsel for all the 
parties he is directed to appear before the counsellors
today itself so that the counsellors take assistance of 
Psychiatrist and the Doctors and interact and make an 
assessment of his mental condition and place the report 
on the next date.
9. Mr. Virk shall handover the videoclips to Mr. 
Dhaundiyal, the Senior Pharmacist, today itself.
10. On the previous date the record of two writ 
petitions WPCRL Nos. 1000 of 2021 and 1613 of 2023 
were also summoned, which are now tagged with this 
file, wherein, the allegation of police atrocities has also  been highlighted.
11. Mr. Saurabh Kuamr Pandey also place before this 
court one of the order of Chief Judicial Magistrate 
dated 25.05.2024 rejecting the application moved under 
section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. moved by one Smt. Pratibha 
Rai W/o Rajan Rai, the resident of Dehradun, making a 
complaint against six police officials including the 
S.H.O. Dharmendra Singh Rautela of P.S. Clementown, 
Dehradun, with the allegation that her son namely 
Prateek was torchered in the police custody. Certain 
photographs have also been enclosed and it has been 
apprised to this court that he was under regular 
treatment and subsequently this young boy of 21 years 
old died.
12. In reference to the aforesaid incident, now a 
revision has been preferred against the order of Chief 
Judicial Magistrate dated 25.05.2024 i.e. Criminal 
Revision No. 219 of 2024, which is pending since 2024 
in the court of 1st Additional District Judge, Dehradun, 
and now the record of revision is being summoned and 
to find out if it is pending since 2024.
13. Registry is directed to summon the entire record 
of Criminal Revision No. 219 of 2024, which is pending 
in the court of 1st Additional District Judge, Dehradun, 
through a Special Messenger and place before this 
court on the next date.
14. Taking into consideration the seriousness of
allegations as alleged all these matters are being kept 
part heard.
15. Put up this matter on 28.04.2026.
16. The petitioner get certain threat in his mobile the 
conversation of which Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey 
already supplied to Mr. Virk, who may also get the 
instructions in this regard.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 24.04.2026

WPCRL No. 589 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey and Mr. Nalin Saun, 
learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy A.G. with Mr. 
Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Pursuant to the previous order the counsellor 
and the Psychiatrist submitted their joint report and as 
per their report the petitioner is medically fit and there 
is no clinical evidence of mental unsoundness and there 
is no disorder and his mental condition is also very 
fine. The report is now kept in the sealed envelope
again.
4. The mother of the petitioner Smt. Urmila Devi 
was also called by the counsellor and she also join 
counsellor today itself and the report is still awaited. 
She is also present in court. This court also interact with 
her and she submits that the First Information Report 
dated 01.05.2025 is infact not on her dictates.
5. On the previous date learned counsel for the 
petitioner bring to the notice of this court one another 
instance of police atrocities in respect of one person 
namely Prateek, who was tortured in the police custody 
and subsequently during treatment he died at the age 
of 21 years and his mother make a complaint against 
six police officials including the then S.H.O. Mr. 
Dharmendra Rautela of P.S. Clementown but her FIR 
was not registered, even the application moved under 
section 156(3) was also rejected against which the 
revision is preferred before the 1st Additional District 
Judge, Dehradun, i.e. Criminal Revision No. 219 of 
2024 but the same is still pending. 
6. The Registry could not take steps to summon the 
record of Criminal Revision No. 219 of 2024 though by 
the order dated 24.04.2026 the Registry was directed to 
summon the entire record of the said revision.
7. Put up this matter as part heard before me on 
04.05.2026.
8. The Registry is directed to send the requisition to  the concerned court forthwith to summon the record of 
the aforesaid criminal revision.
9. In addition to this, Mr. Virk on the next date 
place before this court hand written complaint of the 
mother of the petitioner on the basis of which the chik 
FIR was registered on 01.05.2025.
10. Mr. Virk may complete the instructions by the 
next date.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey and Mr. 
Nalin Saun, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Addl. Advocate 
General along with Mr. Sunil Upadhyaya, 
learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner 
would submit that a Coordinate Bench of 
this Court, vide order dated 08.04.2026, had 
directed the State authorities to preserve the 
C.C.T.V. footage of Koti Colony Outpost, 
Police Station Lambgaon, pertaining to the 
relevant period and to place the same before 
this Court.
4. He would further submit that one Amit, 
learned counsel appearing for respondent 
no. 6 before the trial Court, has allegedly 
uploaded incriminating and objectionable 
material against the petitioner and his 
family members on his Facebook account. In 
support of the said submission, learned 
counsel has produced before the Court a 
printout of the alleged Facebook post. He 
would further place reliance upon the order 
dated 16.04.2026 passed by the Coordinate  Bench, whereby all the parties were directed 
not to post any incriminating material on 
any social media platform. It is contended 
that, despite the aforesaid direction, the said 
advocate has continued to post such 
material on his Facebook account in 
violation of the order passed by this Court.
5. In compliance with the order dated 
08.04.2026, learned State Counsel, on 
instructions, fairly submits that no C.C.T.V. 
camera is installed at Koti Colony Outpost. 
However, he seeks one week's further time to 
ascertain and place on record the availability 
of the C.C.T.V. footage, if any, of Police 
Station Lambgaon for the relevant period. 
Insofar as the allegation regarding the 
publication of incriminating material on the 
Facebook account of the counsel appearing 
for respondent no. 6 is concerned, learned 
State Counsel also seeks time to verify the 
authenticity of the documents produced by 
the petitioner.
6. During the course of hearing, learned 
counsel for the petitioner handed over a 
copy of the printout of the alleged Facebook 
post to learned State Counsel in open Court 
for the purposes of verification.
7. Learned State Counsel is directed to 
verify the aforesaid allegations as well as the 
documents produced by the petitioner and 
place an appropriate report before this Court 
on or before the next date of listing.
8. List this matter on 30.07.2026 along 
with WPCRL No. 1613 of 2023.
9. WPCRL No. 1000 of 2021 and WPCRL 
No. 826 of 2026 shall stand de-linked from 
the present matter, as the said petitions 
have already been decided.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 22-07-2026
